# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

          # Baseline = last green run that exercised ALL legs. A single-leg
          # green dispatch (legs=pubdev inject smoke etc.) must NOT advance
          # the baseline — otherwise the next scheduled run would skip the
          # legs that never ran for that sha.
          last_green=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow daily-publish.yml \
            --branch main --status success --limit 15 \
            --json headSha,event,displayTitle \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.event == "schedule" or (.event == "workflow_dispatch" and (.displayTitle | contains("(all)"))))][0].headSha // empty')
          head=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
          echo "last green daily: ${last_green:-<none>} — main: $head"

          changed=true
          if [ "$last_green" = "$head" ] && [ "$FORCE" != "true" ]; then
            changed=false
            echo "::notice::main has not moved since the last green daily — all legs skip (green-neutral, #159)"
          fi
          echo "changed=$changed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
          next_tag=v0.1.0
          if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
            IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "${latest_tag#v}"
            next_tag="v${major}.${minor}.$((patch + 1))"
          fi
          {
            echo "latest_tag=${latest_tag:-none}"
            echo "next_tag=$next_tag"
            echo "pubspec_version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.

name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: main/tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # Issue #239: TestFlight submit now waits for Apple processing (bounded,
    # default 90 min) + a ~1-min one-shot appearance probe AFTER the
    # build/notarize work (gh-1041: the blocking distribution wait moved to
    # the deferred store-appearance-check workflow) — the job ceiling must
    # cover the worst case, not just the build.
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [arm64, x86_64]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"

          update_mirror() {
            local url="$1"
            local mirror="$2"
            local extra_args="${3:-}"
            if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
              echo "Creating mirror: $mirror"
              if [ -n "$extra_args" ]; then
                # --mirror conflicts with --single-branch/--branch; use --bare
                # for branch-specific mirrors (e.g. flutter_code_editor).
                git clone --bare $extra_args "$url" "$mirror"
              else
                git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
              fi
            else
              echo "Updating mirror: $mirror"
              if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
                rm -rf "$mirror"
                if [ -n "$extra_args" ]; then
                  git clone --bare $extra_args "$url" "$mirror"
                else
                  git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
                fi
              fi
            fi
          }

          update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          echo "Cloning main repo with mirror reference..."
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: |
          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Rust already installed"
            rustup show
          else
            echo "Installing Rust..."
            curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
          fi
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          rustup --version
          cargo --version

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `cli` leg fails — both `Build macOS arm64` and `Build macOS x86_64` jobs die in the step "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" with `The action 'Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework' has timed out after 15 minutes.`

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `build-macos` job, "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step. When neither `actions/cache` nor the runner's local working copy has the framework, the step downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream release asset with `curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`. Two defects compound:

1. **No attempt can ever complete on this link.** The self-hosted runner pulls GitHub release assets at ~300 KB/s (log: ETA `0:05:09` for 92.7M). The full transfer needs ~309 s, but every attempt is capped at `--max-time 240` — and without `-C -` each retry restarts from byte 0, so the download can never finish regardless of how many retries are spent.
2. **The retry budget overruns the step cap (off-by-one).** The step comment budgeted "3 retries × 240s < 900s", but `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt = 4 attempts. Worst case = 4 × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the 900 s** `timeout-minutes: 15` cap. GitHub kills the step mid-attempt-4 (the ticket log shows attempt 4 at ~50% when the 15-minute error fires: step t≈872–940 s, attempt-4 elapsed 2:07–2:55, matching a 735 s attempt-4 start).

Because the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` post-step never saves the framework, so every run on a cold cache repeats the failure — and both matrix arches (serialized on the single self-hosted runner) fail identically, failing the whole `build-macos.yml` child run and with it the daily `cli` leg.

**Impact**: The daily auto-publish `cli` leg (macOS DMG/ZIP release + CLI bundles + extension) fails every day the cache is cold; the self-filing issue (gh-1149) stays open because the leg can never go green.

**Fix approach** (minimum, targeted at the failing step):
- Make retries resumable: add `-C -` so each attempt continues the partial zip from its byte offset (GitHub release assets support Range requests). At the observed ~300 KB/s the download completes during attempt 2 (~315 s).
- Correct the arithmetic: `--retry 2` (3 attempts) → worst case 3 × 240 s + 2 × 5 s + one 30 s connect + unzip ≈ 790 s < 900 s step cap, with the invariant pinned by a test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`).
- `rm -f` the stale `/tmp` zip before downloading so a previous run's leftover can never seed `-C -` with an unknown offset (deterministic fresh start; curl's in-step retries still resume).

**Previous attempt**: None — first filing of gh-1149.

**Out of scope (latent, not failing)**: The four sibling copies of this download (ci.yml ×2, nightly.yml, build-mobile.yml) share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one (4 × 600 s ≫ their 900 s step cap), but they run on GitHub-hosted/ warmed links where attempt 1 completes in well under 600 s, so the worst case never materializes. Left untouched per minimum-fix discipline; build-mobile.yml additionally prefers the runner's local copy and completes attempt 1 at ~309 s on the shared self-hosted link.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

          # Baseline = last green run that exercised ALL legs. A single-leg
          # green dispatch (legs=pubdev inject smoke etc.) must NOT advance
          # the baseline — otherwise the next scheduled run would skip the
          # legs that never ran for that sha.
          last_green=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow daily-publish.yml \
            --branch main --status success --limit 15 \
            --json headSha,event,displayTitle \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.event == "schedule" or (.event == "workflow_dispatch" and (.displayTitle | contains("(all)"))))][0].headSha // empty')
          head=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
          echo "last green daily: ${last_green:-<none>} — main: $head"

          changed=true
          if [ "$last_green" = "$head" ] && [ "$FORCE" != "true" ]; then
            changed=false
            echo "::notice::main has not moved since the last green daily — all legs skip (green-neutral, #159)"
          fi
          echo "changed=$changed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
          next_tag=v0.1.0
          if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
            IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "${latest_tag#v}"
            next_tag="v${major}.${minor}.$((patch + 1))"
          fi
          {
            echo "latest_tag=${latest_tag:-none}"
            echo "next_tag=$next_tag"
            echo "pubspec_version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.

  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────

  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 10 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   220m  →  240m (14400s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 10 → build-android 45 →              85m   →  100m (6000s)  ; 240m

  #   cli        version 10 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      325m  →  340m (20400s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #

name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: main/tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # Issue #239: TestFlight submit now waits for Apple processing (bounded,
    # default 90 min) + a ~1-min one-shot appearance probe AFTER the
    # build/notarize work (gh-1041: the blocking distribution wait moved to
    # the deferred store-appearance-check workflow) — the job ceiling must
    # cover the worst case, not just the build.
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [arm64, x86_64]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"

          update_mirror() {
            local url="$1"
            local mirror="$2"
            local extra_args="${3:-}"
            if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
              echo "Creating mirror: $mirror"
              if [ -n "$extra_args" ]; then
                # --mirror conflicts with --single-branch/--branch; use --bare
                # for branch-specific mirrors (e.g. flutter_code_editor).
                git clone --bare $extra_args "$url" "$mirror"
              else
                git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
              fi
            else
              echo "Updating mirror: $mirror"
              if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
                rm -rf "$mirror"
                if [ -n "$extra_args" ]; then
                  git clone --bare $extra_args "$url" "$mirror"
                else
                  git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
                fi
              fi
            fi
          }

          update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          echo "Cloning main repo with mirror reference..."
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/
          fi

      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):

      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's

      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the

        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup host toolchains

The bug is precisely in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step. Root cause details:

1. The upstream asset is 92.7 MB; on the self-hosted runner's slow link it downloads at ~300 KB/s → needs ~5:09 (309s) — MORE than the per-attempt `--max-time 240`, so EVERY attempt aborts at 240s without completing.
2. `--retry 3` means 3 retries AFTER the initial attempt → 4 total attempts (the comment's math "3 retries × 240s" forgot the initial attempt). Worst case = 4 × 240s + 3 × 5s (retry-delay) = 975s > the step's 900s (timeout-minutes: 15) cap.
3. Since no attempt completes (each capped at 240s < 309s needed) AND the retry budget (975s) exceeds the step timeout (900s), GitHub kills the step during the 4th attempt — "The action ... has timed out after 15 minutes."
4. Because the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` step never saves the framework, so every run on a cold runner repeats this. (The x86_64 matrix leg follows arm64 on the same serialized runner and fails identically.)

Also partial progress is discarded between attempts (no `-C -` resume), so each attempt re-downloads from byte 0.

The fix (minimum targeted): make the download loop fit the step budget deterministically on slow links:
- Use resumable downloads (`curl -C -`) so each attempt makes forward progress.
- Budget: attempts sized so worst case < 900s step cap.

Option A: increase step timeout-minutes and fix curl flags.
Option B: keep timeout-minutes: 15, replace single curl with `--retry 3 --max-time 240` + `-C -` so 4 attempts × 240s resume from previous bytes: attempt1 gets ~72MB (240s × 300KB/s), attempt2 resumes and finishes the remaining ~21MB in ~70s. The hard worst-case bound matters only when the link is so slow that even 4 × 240s can't fetch 92.7MB (i.e. < ~97KB/s). The genuine root cause is twofold:
(a) the per-attempt `--max-time 240` is BELOW the transfer time needed at the observed link speed (~309s), guaranteeing every attempt fails;
(b) the total retry budget (initial + 3 retries) exceeds the 15-min step cap, so the step dies mid-retry-sequence instead of failing fast on curl's own terms — and even if it had "fit", every attempt would still fail because of (a).

So the correct fix must (1) let a single attempt actually complete on a ~300KB/s link (max-time ≥ ~360-420s, or resume support), and (2) keep the aggregate retry budget strictly under the step cap with correct arithmetic (attempts = retries + 1).

Let me nail down the exact root cause numbers once more:

build-macos.yml step:
```yaml
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          ...
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
              -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
              https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
```

- Asset: 92.7 MB (log: `92.7M`).
- Observed rate: ~300 KB/s → full transfer needs ≈ 309s (5:09, exactly what curl's ETA column showed: `0:05:09`).
- Per-attempt cap `--max-time 240` < 309s → EVERY attempt aborts at 240s having fetched only ~72MB (78%).
- `--retry 3` = initial attempt + 3 retries = 4 attempts, not 3 (the comment's "3 retries × 240s" arithmetic forgot the initial attempt).
- Worst-case curl wall time = 4 × 240s + 3 × 5s (retry-delay) = 975s > 900s step cap (timeout-minutes: 15).
- Each retry restarts from byte 0 (no `-C -`), so nothing makes forward progress.
- Result: GitHub runner kills the step during the 4th attempt → `##[error]The action 'Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework' has timed out after 15 minutes.` The log excerpt shows the 4th attempt at ~48-55% downloaded when killed (each attempt dies at 240s ≈ 41-48%... hmm wait, the log lines show 41-55%, at elapsed 2:07-2:55 within the visible window).

Hmm wait, actually let me re-derive which attempt the visible log lines belong to. The step starts at some T0. The error fired at 07:15:22 with "timed out after 15 minutes" — so the step began ≈ 07:00:22. Visible lines: 07:14:33 → 07:15:22 = 872s → 940s into the step. Within a curl attempt showing elapsed 2:07 (127s) → 2:55 (175s). If this is attempt 4: attempt 4 starts at 3 × (240 + 5) = 735s. 872 - 735 = 137s ≈ 2:17... close to the 2:07-2:55 range shown. ✓. And 55% ≈ 51MB at 300KB/s ≈ 170s ✓. So yes — attempt 4 killed at the 900s step cap. Perfectly consistent.

Also worth noting: the comment in the workflow says the budget was designed as "3 retries × 240s max-time + connect + unzip < 900s" — the design intended 3 attempts × 240 = 720s ≤ 900s, but `--retry 3` gives 4 attempts. AND even 720s budget wouldn't help because each attempt is capped below the transfer time — the design conflated "per-attempt cap" with "total transfer budget". With no resume, the transfer can NEVER complete at ~300KB/s regardless of retries. So two defects:
1. Per-attempt max-time (240s) below the link's needed transfer time (~309s) with no `-C -` resume → download can never succeed on this link.
2. Retry arithmetic off by one (4 attempts, 975s > 900s step cap) → the step timeout fires mid-retry instead of curl failing (or succeeding) within its own budget.

Fix design (minimum, targeted at this step):
- Make each attempt resumable: `curl -L -C -` so retries continue from the byte offset (GitHub release assets support Range).
- Re-derive the budget with correct arithmetic so worst case + unzip fits the step cap: keep `timeout-minutes: 15` (900s) and use `--retry 2 --max-time 240` → 3 attempts × 240 + 2 × 5 = 730s ≤ 900s with ~170s for connect/unzip/slack. With resume: attempt1 fetches ~72MB (240s), attempt2 fetches remaining ~21MB in ~70s → completes at ~315s total. Even at 150KB/s: 3 attempts × 36MB = 108MB ≥ 92.7MB → completes at ~720s < 730s budget. At <~103KB/s (3×240×103KB = 74MB < 92.7MB) it would still fail — but that's 3× slower than anything observed; the cache hit path covers steady state.

Hmm, alternatively bump the step timeout to 20m and keep more retries. Which is more in the spirit of "minimum targeted fix"? The step currently has timeout-minutes: 15. The daily-publish budget arithmetic (#351) uses job-level 150m ceilings, not step-level, so bumping the step to 20m is harmless to that math.

I'll do both safety margins:
- `-C -` resume (the key defect fix: forward progress)
- Correct the arithmetic: budget = attempts × max-time + (attempts-1) × retry-delay < (timeout-minutes × 60) − margin.

Decision: keep step timeout 15m; curl: `--retry 2 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 -C -`. Worst case 730s + connect (30s once) + unzip (~15s) ≈ 775s < 900s ✓. At the observed 300KB/s the transfer completes during attempt 2 (~315s). 

Hmm, wait — one more consideration on `-C -` behavior: when curl retries due to --retry with `-C -`, does it actually resume? Let me double-check curl's documented semantics. From curl man page (CURLOPT_RESUME_FROM_LARGE / -C): "-C, --continue-at <offset>: Continue/Resume a previous file transfer at the given offset." And --retry: "If a transfer times out (curlopt_timeout / --max-time)... transient error... curl will retry". The interplay: on retry, curl restarts the transfer; with -C -, the restart uses the current size of the output file as the offset. This is a well-known pattern (`curl -C --retry 10 ...`). Yes, retries honor -C -. 

One more subtlety: with `-C -` and `-o file`, if the server returns a non-resumable response or the file doesn't exist yet, curl starts from 0. Fine.

Also the server redirect chain (github.com → objects.githubusercontent.com): both support Range. The `-L` keeps following. OK.

That's acceptable and arguably desired (fail fast, next run's cache miss re-downloads). But we could add integrity awareness... Keep minimal.

Both matrix jobs serialize on the same runner; each has its own workspace and downloads separately (the actions/cache post-save from arm64's job may make x86_64's cache hit IF arm64's job completes first and cache save happens — cache is saved in the post-action of the job... they run in parallel (matrix jobs are separate), both one runner serialized. arm64 runs first; after its job, cache save; then x86_64 hits the cache. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `cli` leg fails — both `Build macOS arm64` and `Build macOS x86_64` jobs die in the step "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" with `The action 'Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework' has timed out after 15 minutes.`

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `build-macos` job, "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step. When neither `actions/cache` nor the runner's local working copy has the framework, the step downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream release asset with `curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`. Two defects compound:

1. **No attempt can ever complete on this link.** The self-hosted runner pulls GitHub release assets at ~300 KB/s (log: ETA `0:05:09` for 92.7M). The full transfer needs ~309 s, but every attempt is capped at `--max-time 240` — and without `-C -` each retry restarts from byte 0, so the download can never finish regardless of how many retries are spent.
2. **The retry budget overruns the step cap (off-by-one).** The step comment budgeted "3 retries × 240s < 900s", but `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt = 4 attempts. Worst case = 4 × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the 900 s** `timeout-minutes: 15` cap. GitHub kills the step mid-attempt-4 (the ticket log shows attempt 4 at ~50% when the 15-minute error fires: step t≈872–940 s, attempt-4 elapsed 2:07–2:55, matching a 735 s attempt-4 start).

Because the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` post-step never saves the framework, so every run on a cold cache repeats the failure — and both matrix arches (serialized on the single self-hosted runner) fail identically, failing the whole `build-macos.yml` child run and with it the daily `cli` leg.

**Impact**: The daily auto-publish `cli` leg (macOS DMG/ZIP release + CLI bundles + extension) fails every day the cache is cold; the self-filing issue (gh-1149) stays open because the leg can never go green.

**Fix approach** (minimum, targeted at the failing step):
- Make retries resumable: add `-C -` so each attempt continues the partial zip from its byte offset (GitHub release assets support Range requests). At the observed ~300 KB/s the download completes during attempt 2 (~315 s).
- Correct the arithmetic: `--retry 2` (3 attempts) → worst case 3 × 240 s + 2 × 5 s + one 30 s connect + unzip ≈ 790 s < 900 s step cap, with the invariant pinned by a test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`).
- `rm -f` the stale `/tmp` zip before downloading so a previous run's leftover can never seed `-C -` with an unknown offset (deterministic fresh start; curl's in-step retries still resume).

**Previous attempt**: None — first filing of gh-1149.

**Out of scope (latent, not failing)**: The four sibling copies of this download (ci.yml ×2, nightly.yml, build-mobile.yml) share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one (4 × 600 s ≫ their 900 s step cap), but they run on GitHub-hosted/ warmed links where attempt 1 completes in well under 600 s, so the worst case never materializes. Left untouched per minimum-fix discipline; build-mobile.yml additionally prefers the runner's local copy and completes attempt 1 at ~309 s on the shared self-hosted link.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

          # Baseline = last green run that exercised ALL legs. A single-leg
          # green dispatch (legs=pubdev inject smoke etc.) must NOT advance
          # the baseline — otherwise the next scheduled run would skip the
          # legs that never ran for that sha.
          last_green=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow daily-publish.yml \
            --branch main --status success --limit 15 \
            --json headSha,event,displayTitle \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.event == "schedule" or (.event == "workflow_dispatch" and (.displayTitle | contains("(all)"))))][0].headSha // empty')
          head=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
          echo "last green daily: ${last_green:-<none>} — main: $head"

          changed=true
          if [ "$last_green" = "$head" ] && [ "$FORCE" != "true" ]; then
            changed=false
            echo "::notice::main has not moved since the last green daily — all legs skip (green-neutral, #159)"
          fi
          echo "changed=$changed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
          next_tag=v0.1.0
          if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
            IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "${latest_tag#v}"
            next_tag="v${major}.${minor}.$((patch + 1))"
          fi
          {
            echo "latest_tag=${latest_tag:-none}"
            echo "next_tag=$next_tag"
            echo "pubspec_version=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.

# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list

run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: main/tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]

    # cover the worst case, not just the build.

      fail-fast: false

    permissions:
      contents: write

      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"

          update_mirror() {
            local url="$1"
            local mirror="$2"
            local extra_args="${3:-}"
            if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
              echo "Creating mirror: $mirror"
              if [ -n "$extra_args" ]; then
                # --mirror conflicts with --single-branch/--branch; use --bare
                # for branch-specific mirrors (e.g. flutter_code_editor).
                git clone --bare $extra_args "$url" "$mirror"
              else
                git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
              fi
            else
              echo "Updating mirror: $mirror"
              if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"

                  git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
                fi
              fi

          }

          update_mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |

(b) the total retry budget (initial + 3 retries) exceeds the 15-min step cap, so the step dies mid-retry-sequence instead of failing fast on curl's own terms — and even if it had "fit", every attempt would still fail because of (a).

So the correct fix must (1) let a single attempt actually complete on a ~300KB/s link (max-time ≥ ~360-420s, or resume support), and (2) keep the aggregate retry budget strictly under the step cap with correct arithmetic (attempts = retries + 1).

Design: 
- Step timeout: bump 15 → 20 (headroom for unzip of the 93MB zip and connect timeouts).
- curl: `--retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 420 -C -`
  - attempts = 4; worst case 4 × 420 + 3 × 5 = 1695s > 1200s. NO — that breaks the arithmetic again in the absolute worst case. Need worst_case_total ≤ step budget with margin for connect+unzip.

Let me do the arithmetic properly. Step budget 1200s. Reserve: unzip ~30-60s (93MB zip → maybe 200MB+; unzip is fast, ~10-30s), connect 30s, misc ~30s. Budget for curl ≤ ~1080s.

With resume (`-C -`), what matters is TOTAL transfer time needed = 92.7MB / rate. For the step to succeed at rate r: 92.7MB/r ≤ curl_budget. At 300KB/s → 309s. At 200KB/s → 464s. At 150KB/s → 620s. At 128KB/s → 725s.

curl budget with A attempts of max-time M each: A×M + (A-1)×5 ≤ 1080.
- 3 × 360 + 10 = 1090 (≈ tight). At 360s/attempt and 3 attempts: per-attempt 360s; total transfer capability at 300KB/s = 3 × 108MB = 324MB ≫ 93MB, and total time to fetch 93MB at 300KB/s = 309s — the FIRST attempt finishes (309 < 360). At 150KB/s: attempt1 54MB, attempt2 +54 = 108 > 93 → done during attempt 2 (620s total < 720s budget). 
- Worst case full 3 × 360 = 1090s ≤ 1200s ✓ (leaves 110s for unzip+slack — unzip 93MB is ~5-15s on macOS; fine).

`--retry 2` = 2 retries + 1 initial = 3 attempts. 3 × 360s + 2 × 5s = 1090s ≤ 1200s ✓.

Hmm, but wait — is `-C -` with `--retry` actually needed, or does curl's --retry itself resume? No — curl's built-in --retry does NOT resume by default; it restarts the transfer (unless `-C -` is specified, in which case retries resume from the offset — actually let me verify: curl man: "--retry ... When curl is about to retry a transfer, it will first wait one second and then for all forthcoming retries it will double the waiting time until it reaches 10 minutes... " and for -C: "Use '-C -' to tell curl to automatically find out where/how to resume the transfer.". The combination `curl -C --retry N` makes each retry resume the previous partial output file. Yes, that's a known pattern; curl retries honor -C - and continue from the existing file size. Confirmed by curl docs/behavior: retry transfers respect --continue-at.

One subtlety: with `-o file` and `-C -`, if the file is already complete, curl says "The file is already fully retrieved; nothing to do." and exits... code 0? Modern curl exits 0 in that case? Hmm — I recall it exits with 0 since it's not an error... Actually there are reports: curl 7.x prints "The file is already fully retrieved; nothing to do." and exits with status 0? Let me check: the message is in main.c when (inresumable scenario) — `curl --continue-at -` with a fully downloaded file exits 0 historically. Hmm, actually I remember curl returns exit code 0 for "already fully retrieved". Not 100% certain across versions. In our flow this shouldn't trigger anyway (each successful curl is followed by unzip; a second curl would only run in a fresh step). Within one step, the loop is curl's internal retry — after success it stops. So the "already fully retrieved" case can only arise on a step re-run after a completed download but failed unzip — rare; and if curl exits non-zero there, `set -e` fails the step with a clear message. Acceptable.

GitHub release assets support Range requests (served from S3 with accept-ranges: bytes). Confirmed knowledge: `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/...` redirects to `objects.githubusercontent.com` which supports byte ranges. Yes.

Also there's the actions/cache before this step — on cache hit, no download. The cache is only saved after a successful job (post step). So fixing the step also fixes the cache-population problem going forward: first green run after the fix warms the cache, subsequent runs hit it.

But ALSO: why did the cache miss in the first place? Key `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` is static. On a self-hosted runner with persistent disk, actions/cache stores under `~/.actions-cache` or the runner's work dir...…

```yaml

            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \

AND even 720s budget wouldn't help because each attempt is capped below the transfer time — the design conflated "per-attempt cap" with "total transfer budget". With no resume, the transfer can NEVER complete at ~300KB/s regardless of retries. So two defects:
1. Per-attempt max-time (240s) below the link's needed transfer time (~309s) with no `-C -` resume → download can never succeed on this link.
2. Retry arithmetic off by one (4 attempts, 975s > 900s step cap) → the step timeout fires mid-retry instead of curl failing (or succeeding) within its own budget.

- `-C -` resume (the key defect fix: forward progress)

From curl man page (CURLOPT_RESUME_FROM_LARGE / -C): "-C, --continue-at <offset>: Continue/Resume a previous file transfer at the given offset." And --retry: "If a transfer times out (curlopt_timeout / --max-time)... transient error... curl will retry". The interplay: on retry, curl restarts the transfer; with -C -, the restart uses the current size of the output file as the offset. This is a well-known pattern (`curl -C --retry 10 ...`).
