# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +266
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:28:42Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -

```

expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:

```

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. ```

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"

          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"

            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip

Oops — I used double-quoted Dart strings, so `${{ matrix.arch }}` and `$ZIP` interpolate. Fix: escape the `$` in double-quoted strings, or use raw/single-quoted strings. Single-quoted Dart strings don't interpolate `$`... wait, actually in Dart, single-quoted strings DO interpolate `$` too! Dart string interpolation works in both single and double quotes ('...' and "..."), NOT in raw strings (r'...'). So I need to escape: `\$` in normal strings, or use raw strings `r'...'` where the content has no other escapes needed.

For `contains('ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"')` → use raw string: `r'ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"'`. Raw strings are ideal.

For `contains('rm -f "$ZIP"')` → `r'rm -f "$ZIP"'`.
For the digest echo line → `r'echo "$digest  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'` — hmm but the string also contains the Dart-interpolated digest... I wrote `'echo "$digest  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'` where `$digest` was intended to interpolate the Dart const digest. That's actually what I want: Dart interpolates `$digest` → the digest value, and then literal `  $ZIP` in the workflow. So only `$ZIP` needs escaping: `'echo "$digest  \$ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'`.
For `'unzip -q "$ZIP"'` → `r'unzip -q "$ZIP"'` or `'unzip -q "\$ZIP"'`.

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"

            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip

Oops — I used double-quoted Dart strings, so `${{ matrix.arch }}` and `$ZIP` interpolate. Fix: escape the `$` in double-quoted strings, or use raw/single-quoted strings. Single-quoted Dart strings don't interpolate `$`... wait, actually in Dart, single-quoted strings DO interpolate `$` too! Dart string interpolation works in both single and double quotes ('...' and "..."), NOT in raw strings (r'...'). So I need to escape: `\$` in normal strings, or use raw strings `r'...'` where the content has no other escapes needed.

For `contains('ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"')` → use raw string: `r'ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"'`. Raw strings are ideal.

For `contains('rm -f "$ZIP"')` → `r'rm -f "$ZIP"'`.
For the digest echo line → `r'echo "$digest  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'` — hmm but the string also contains the Dart-interpolated digest... I wrote `'echo "$digest  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'` where `$digest` was intended to interpolate the Dart const digest. That's actually what I want: Dart interpolates `$digest` → the digest value, and then literal `  $ZIP` in the workflow. So only `$ZIP` needs escaping: `'echo "$digest  \$ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'`.
For `'unzip -q "$ZIP"'` → `r'unzip -q "$ZIP"'` or `'unzip -q "\$ZIP"'`.

arguments.patch:
[.github/workflows/build-macos.yml#AB32]
SWAP 343.=357:
+            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
+            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
+            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
+            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
+            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
+            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
+            rm -f "$ZIP"
+            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+              # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
+              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
+              # engages this loop's retries and the explicit failure below.
+              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
+                -o "$ZIP" \
+                https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
+                break
+              fi
+              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
+                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
+                exit 1
+              fi
+              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
+              sleep 5
+            done
+            # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
+            # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
+            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
+            # as the litertlm download above).
+            echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -
+            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. ```

Oops — I used double-quoted Dart strings, so `${{ matrix.arch }}` and `$ZIP` interpolate. Fix: escape the `$` in double-quoted strings, or use raw/single-quoted strings. Single-quoted Dart strings don't interpolate `$`... wait, actually in Dart, single-quoted strings DO interpolate `$` too! Dart string interpolation works in both single and double quotes ('...' and "..."), NOT in raw strings (r'...'). So I need to escape: `\$` in normal strings, or use raw strings `r'...'` where the content has no other escapes needed.

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.

To make a bounded, resumable download, own the retries in a bash loop and give curl only `-C - --max-time <budget>`; `rm -f` the partial file before the loop so `-C -` resumes only your own bytes. Budget arithmetic for GH Actions: attempts*max_time + (attempts-1)*sleep must fit the step's timeout-minutes (remember curl `--retry N` means N retries PLUS the initial attempt).","tags":["ci","github-actions","curl","networking","workflows","gotcha"]}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +266
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:28:42Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: verify the downloaded zip against a pinned sha256 (like the sibling step does)**

The flutter_gemma step 90 lines up in this same file downloads its asset and immediately pins it: `shasum -a 256 -c -` against a hardcoded digest. This download — a 92.7 MB asset that (per gh-1149) will routinely arrive in resumed pieces — has no integrity check beyond `unzip` CRC32. CRC catches torn writes, but not a *wrong-content-but-valid-zip* (asset re-uploaded under the same tag, proxy/intercepted payload), which would then be cached forever under `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`.

The release asset is immutable per tag, so a one-liner after the loop makes the step self-verifying:

```bash
echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -
unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
```

---

### Thread 4 — `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: also pin `break` — it is load-bearing for the success path**

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. The three current tests stay green through that regression.

One cheap assertion in the first test (alongside the `--retry` one):

```dart
expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:
    'a successful attempt must exit the loop — without break the next '
    '-C - attempt hits HTTP 416 on the complete file and fails the step');
```

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
## Automated Code Review — COMMENT (no blockers)

**Summary**: Root cause and fix are correct and match the ticket: the budget arithmetic checks out (3 × 240s + 2 × 5s = 730s, +60s reserve ≤ 900s cap), `-C -` resume is present, `rm -f` seeds a fresh partial, and the failure path is explicit. Verified locally at HEAD `1e56bcf0f`: the new static lint passes 3/3, `dart analyze` and `dart format` are clean.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: both matrix archs share `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`; they run on one self-hosted runner and have raced shared state before (keychain, line 361) — use a per-arch temp name
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: add `--fail` to curl — without it HTTP 404/5xx exit 0, bypass the retry loop, and land an error page in the zip
- 💡 SUGGESTION: pin a sha256 for the download (same pattern as the flutter_gemma step in this file); pin `break` in the lint test
- 💡 SUGGESTION: the "latent sites" note in the PR description is incomplete — `build-macos.yml:265` (same file) and `ci.yml` ×3 (not ×2, incl. the iOS WasmRun leg at :1686) share the no-resume/off-by-one `--retry 3 --max-time 600` pattern; please file the follow-up with the full list

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +266
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:28:42Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash

... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -

```

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:

```

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: verify the downloaded zip against a pinned sha256 (like the sibling step does)**

The flutter_gemma step 90 lines up in this same file downloads its asset and immediately pins it: `shasum -a 256 -c -` against a hardcoded digest. This download — a 92.7 MB asset that (per gh-1149) will routinely arrive in resumed pieces — has no integrity check beyond `unzip` CRC32. CRC catches torn writes, but not a *wrong-content-but-valid-zip* (asset re-uploaded under the same tag, proxy/intercepted payload), which would then be cached forever under `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`.

The release asset is immutable per tag, so a one-liner after the loop makes the step self-verifying:

```bash
echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -
unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
```

---

### Thread 4 — `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: also pin `break` — it is load-bearing for the success path**

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. The three current tests stay green through that regression.

One cheap assertion in the first test (alongside the `--retry` one):

```dart
expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:
    'a successful attempt must exit the loop — without break the next '
    '-C - attempt hits HTTP 416 on the complete file and fails the step');
```

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
## Automated Code Review — COMMENT (no blockers)

**Summary**: Root cause and fix are correct and match the ticket: the budget arithmetic checks out (3 × 240s + 2 × 5s = 730s, +60s reserve ≤ 900s cap), `-C -` resume is present, `rm -f` seeds a fresh partial, and the failure path is explicit. Verified locally at HEAD `1e56bcf0f`: the new static lint passes 3/3, `dart analyze` and `dart format` are clean.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: both matrix archs share `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`; they run on one self-hosted runner and have raced shared state before (keychain, line 361) — use a per-arch temp name

          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"

          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. ### Notes

          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"

          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip

Oops — I used double-quoted Dart strings, so `${{ matrix.arch }}` and `$ZIP` interpolate. Fix: escape the `$` in double-quoted strings, or use raw/single-quoted strings. Single-quoted Dart strings don't interpolate `$`... wait, actually in Dart, single-quoted strings DO interpolate `$` too! Dart string interpolation works in both single and double quotes ('...' and "..."), NOT in raw strings (r'...'). So I need to escape: `\$` in normal strings, or use raw strings `r'...'` where the content has no other escapes needed.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +266
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:28:42Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: verify the downloaded zip against a pinned sha256 (like the sibling step does)**

The flutter_gemma step 90 lines up in this same file downloads its asset and immediately pins it: `shasum -a 256 -c -` against a hardcoded digest. This download — a 92.7 MB asset that (per gh-1149) will routinely arrive in resumed pieces — has no integrity check beyond `unzip` CRC32. ```bash
echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -

```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: also pin `break` — it is load-bearing for the success path**

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. ```dart
expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:

```

          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1154._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

```bash
rm -f "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
... -o "/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip" ...
```

and update the `rm -f` pin in the test to match. (`mktemp` works too; `unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"` accordingly.)

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: verify the downloaded zip against a pinned sha256 (like the sibling step does)**

The flutter_gemma step 90 lines up in this same file downloads its asset and immediately pins it: `shasum -a 256 -c -` against a hardcoded digest. This download — a 92.7 MB asset that (per gh-1149) will routinely arrive in resumed pieces — has no integrity check beyond `unzip` CRC32. CRC catches torn writes, but not a *wrong-content-but-valid-zip* (asset re-uploaded under the same tag, proxy/intercepted payload), which would then be cached forever under `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0`.

The release asset is immutable per tag, so a one-liner after the loop makes the step self-verifying:

```bash
echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -
unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
```

---

### Thread 4 — `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
💡 **SUGGESTION: also pin `break` — it is load-bearing for the success path**

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. The three current tests stay green through that regression.

One cheap assertion in the first test (alongside the `--retry` one):

```dart
expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:
    'a successful attempt must exit the loop — without break the next '
    '-C - attempt hits HTTP 416 on the complete file and fails the step');
```

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
## Automated Code Review — COMMENT (no blockers)

**Summary**: Root cause and fix are correct and match the ticket: the budget arithmetic checks out (3 × 240s + 2 × 5s = 730s, +60s reserve ≤ 900s cap), `-C -` resume is present, `rm -f` seeds a fresh partial, and the failure path is explicit. Verified locally at HEAD `1e56bcf0f`: the new static lint passes 3/3, `dart analyze` and `dart format` are clean.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: both matrix archs share `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`; they run on one self-hosted runner and have raced shared state before (keychain, line 361) — use a per-arch temp name
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: add `--fail` to curl — without it HTTP 404/5xx exit 0, bypass the retry loop, and land an error page in the zip
- 💡 SUGGESTION: pin a sha256 for the download (same pattern as the flutter_gemma step in this file); pin `break` in the lint test

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              if curl -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
                https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
              sleep 5
            done
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).

Oops — I used double-quoted Dart strings, so `${{ matrix.arch }}` and `$ZIP` interpolate. Fix: escape the `$` in double-quoted strings, or use raw/single-quoted strings. Single-quoted Dart strings don't interpolate `$`... wait, actually in Dart, single-quoted strings DO interpolate `$` too! Dart string interpolation works in both single and double quotes ('...' and "..."), NOT in raw strings (r'...'). So I need to escape: `\$` in normal strings, or use raw strings `r'...'` where the content has no other escapes needed.

For `contains('ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"')` → use raw string: `r'ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"'`. Raw strings are ideal.

{"content":"### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.

To make a bounded, resumable download, own the retries in a bash loop and give curl only `-C - --max-time <budget>`; `rm -f` the partial file before the loop so `-C -` resumes only your own bytes. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +266
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:28:42Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: shared `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` races between the two matrix arch jobs**

In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

- Job A's `rm -f` unlinks Job B's in-flight partial; Job B's next `-C -` attempt and Job A's curl then write the **same path** concurrently → interleaved bytes → `unzip` CRC failure (confusing transient red, not silent corruption).
- Before this PR the download could never succeed anyway, so the race was unreachable; this change makes it the live success path.
- The new test (`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart:206`) pins the shared name verbatim, making the later fix harder.

Fix (one line) — make the temp file per-arch:

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

echo "<pinned-sha256>  /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip" | shasum -a 256 -c -

```

The lint pins `--max-time`, the single retry layer, `-C -`, and the fresh seed, but not the `break` on success. If `break` is ever dropped during refactoring, a *successful* first download falls through to attempt 2: `-C -` against an already-complete file gets HTTP 416 → curl exits 33 → the loop reads success as failure → `exit 1` after 3 attempts despite holding a complete zip. expect(loop.body, contains('break'), reason:

```

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — all green (see run log); neighboring workflow lints (`release_hygiene`, `dispatch_watch`, `store_appearance_check`, `setup_flutter_selfhosted`, `store_automation_guard`): 137 passed.

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
